findings.title: Correct the CDQ83_07225 coupling-enzyme preparation and its evidence
findings.observation: The qualifier says auxiliary-enzyme ammonium sulfate was removed by ultrafiltration. The 2020 Methods instead specify lyophilized rabbit aldolase/GPDH and explain that the earlier ammonium-sulfate suspensions could not be used with S7P barium salt. Ultrafiltration in the neighboring paragraph applies to the purified PFK buffer exchange. The qualifier cites 2019 preparation paragraphs, which do not establish the 2020 added-ammonium condition.
findings.correction: State that the 2020 assay used lyophilized auxiliary enzymes in place of the earlier ammonium-sulfate suspensions, retaining BaSO4 precipitation and the source NH4Cl2 inconsistency. Cite the actual 2020 Methods in the qualifier; preserve the separate 2019 His6/TEV construct evidence.
findings.acceptance: No claim that auxiliary enzymes were ultrafiltered remains. The qualifier includes the 2020 assay paragraph and keeps CDQ83_07225/F6P/ATP scope; no PPi-S7P catalytic edge is added.
findings.rationale: The ammonium activation result is supported; the incorrect preparation mechanism is peripheral provenance, not a wrong catalyst or sign.

findings.title: Separate the Pfp mixed-substrate activity assay from the MS identity experiment
findings.observation: The draft calls the mixed F6P/S7P competition measurement an MS assay. The primary Results say that the competition assay monitored FBP production, and the Pfp Methods describe the coupled activity assays. The separate MS Methods contain S7P alone for product identification. The inaccessible supplementary Table S3 is not a basis for asserting an MS competition readout.
findings.correction: Replace mixed-substrate MS assay with mixed-substrate FBP activity assay; add the Pfp assay Methods locator if specifying the coupled readout. Keep the observed decrease and the explicitly interpretive competition explanation.
findings.acceptance: The S7P inhibition edge still refers only to reduced F6P-to-FBP activity with mixed substrates; it does not assert binding affinity or suppression of S7P catalysis.
findings.rationale: The sign and substrate scope survive; only the measurement modality was overstated.

findings.title: Use the actual titles of the 1982 and 2022 primary articles
findings.observation: Both title fields contain descriptive substitutes. The 1982 original first-page scan is titled A pathway for the interconversion of hexose and pentose in the parasitic amoeba Entamoeba histolytica. The retained 2022 publisher rendering is titled Increasing the Thermodynamic Driving Force of the Phosphofructokinase Reaction in Clostridium thermocellum.
locators: Retained publisher rendering, initial title line
findings.correction: Replace the two title strings with the inspected original titles; retain the existing identifiers, URLs, artifact bindings and access limitations.
findings.acceptance: Both titles match the originals after whitespace normalization; no reference identity or source hash is silently replaced.
findings.rationale: The sources themselves are the correct papers, so this is bibliographic provenance rather than wrong biological evidence.

findings.title: Carry the six known reversible directions into reaction metadata
findings.observation: Every original Reaction has reaction-direction REVERSIBLE, and the prose and side evidence correctly retain it. All six record reaction nodes omit direction, so the native node/graph/export direction field is unavailable despite known source support.
findings.correction: Set direction: reversible on each of the six existing reaction nodes. Keep the selected pathway-layout side orientations and all twenty side occurrences exactly as authored.
findings.acceptance: All six node directions are reversible; the 51 edge triples and 20 side triples remain unchanged. Standalone/native page and KGX node metadata expose the direction after regeneration.
findings.rationale: No current edge falsely states irreversibility; this is loss of supported structured metadata, not a wrong chemical route.

findings.title: Bind construct features to the exact tested enzyme and nearest primary passage
findings.observation: ppi-034 asserts the His6/TEV construct but cites only the 2020 Methods and issuing native sequence; the retained 2019 Methods directly establish that feature. Aldoa linker wording is supported by the 2023 Results, but those Results are omitted from the qualifier locators. For Pfp, the inspected 2023 Methods explicitly call PfkA, PfkB and Aldoa codon optimized, then refer Pfp to an earlier study; the Pfp-specific text and thesis establish His6 but do not explicitly establish its linker or codon optimization. Those features should not be transferred from neighboring proteins.
findings.correction: Add the retained 2019 direct construct citation to ppi-034. Add the actual Aldoa linker Results locator to the four Aldoa qualifiers. For Pfp, keep the supported pAHCT0347/pRSET-A, His6, host, strain and assay distinctions, while making the linker/codon-optimization uncertainty explicit or supplying an inspected Pfp-specific construct source before retaining those extra features.
findings.acceptance: Every retained construct feature is entailed by its cited exact passage for that enzyme. No unsupported Pfp linker/codon-optimization assertion remains; all biological endpoints, catalytic activities, signs, strains and negative controls are preserved.
findings.rationale: Correct His-tagged engineered preparations are already recognized. The gaps concern exact auxiliary construct features and direct evidence placement.
